title: Avengers: Doomsday Earns $16.5 Million in Record-Breaking First-Day Pre-Sales
excerpt: Marvel's next Avengers installment posted the third-highest 24-hour pre-sale total in the post-pandemic era — from only 1,000 theaters and without IMAX — signaling massive demand for the December blockbuster.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Avengers: Doomsday earned $16.5 million in first-day pre-sales, more than double Deadpool & Wolverine.
  • The film's pre-sales rank third-highest for post-pandemic releases, behind two Spider-Man films.
  • Set for a December 18 release, it features Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom and aims for $230-$260 million opening.
  • Pre-sales occurred at only 1,000 theaters, just 10% of total screens for the film's release.
  • In India, over 159,000 users expressed interest in the film before its release.

  • Avengers: Doomsday generated $10.5 million in advance ticket sales within its first 12 hours and $16.5 million within 24 hours, more than double Deadpool & Wolverine's first-day pre-sales.
  • The film posted the third-highest 24-hour pre-sale kickoff for any post-COVID release, behind only Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Spider-Man: No Way Home, despite tickets being available at just 1,000 premium-format theaters.
  • Set for a December 18 release, the Russo brothers-directed film features Robert Downey Jr.'s return to the MCU as Doctor Doom and is forecast to open between $230 million and $260 million domestically.

Record-Breaking Pre-Sales on Limited Screens

Avengers: Doomsday shattered advance ticket sales records within hours of bookings going live on July 20, generating an estimated $10.5 million in its first 12 hours and reaching $16.5 million by the end of its first full day, according to Variety and box office tracker Sacnilk. The figures are particularly striking because tickets were only available for Disney's new Infinity Vision premium large-format screens at roughly 1,000 domestic theaters — just 10% of the total screens that will carry the film at release.

The haul more than doubled the first-day pre-sales of Deadpool & Wolverine and surpassed the entire first-day bookings of Captain America: Brave New World, Thunderbolts, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps within just two hours. Showtimes for the film's opening on December 17 and 18 were largely sold out, prompting theaters to add screenings for Christmas Day and beyond.

Third-Biggest Post-COVID Pre-Sale Kickoff

According to box office analyst Luiz Fernando, Doomsday's 24-hour pre-sale performance ranked as the third-highest for any post-pandemic release, trailing only two Spider-Man films: Brand New Day and No Way Home. The film narrowly edged out Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, despite having no access to IMAX bookings — a format that typically drives a significant share of advance ticket revenue.

The pre-sales coincided with the release of the film's first full trailer, which showcased Robert Downey Jr.'s transformation into Doctor Doom and teased reunions between original Avengers members, including Thor and Steve Rogers. The trailer quickly became one of the most-discussed entertainment events of the week.

A Pivotal Moment for the MCU

The fifth Avengers installment arrives at a critical juncture for the Marvel Cinematic Universe. While the franchise has delivered hits like Spider-Man: No Way Home and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 since Endgame, several releases — Eternals, Thor: Love and Thunder, and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania — underwhelmed at the box office. With a reported production budget of $400 million and a marketing spend of $300 million, Doomsday will need roughly $1.5 billion worldwide just to break even.

Long-range forecasts project a North American opening weekend of $230 million to $260 million — short of Endgame's $357 million domestic debut but firmly in blockbuster territory. The film's 165-minute runtime makes it the second-longest MCU entry after Endgame.

India and the Diaspora Angle

In India, anticipation is already running high. BookMyShow listed over 159,000 users as "interested" in the film days before its December release, and Indian social media erupted with debate after the trailer dropped — with many comparing Doomsday's visual effects to the recently unveiled Ramayana teaser from Nitesh Tiwari. The discussion reflected growing confidence in homegrown visual spectacles even as the MCU retains its massive Indian fanbase. The Russo brothers are no strangers to Indian box office dominance; Endgame remains a cultural touchstone in the country, and Koimoi reported that the directors are eyeing the No. 1 all-time spot in India with Doomsday, potentially overtaking James Cameron's records.

What's Next

Doomsday faces a formidable opponent at the December 18 box office: Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three, which has reportedly locked a three-week IMAX exclusive window. Disney's Infinity Vision format is widely seen as a strategic counter to secure premium screens for Marvel. Regular IMAX, standard-format, and international ticket sales have yet to open, meaning the current pre-sale figures represent only a fraction of eventual demand.

Directed by Joe and Anthony Russo and featuring an ensemble of over 30 confirmed actors — including Chris Hemsworth, Florence Pugh, Pedro Pascal, Ian McKellen, and Anthony Mackie — Avengers: Doomsday is set to kick off the final chapter of the Multiverse Saga, with Avengers: Secret Wars following on December 17, 2027.
